ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.claim: The closing section resumes the opening themes of monotheism and the Hereafter and assures the Prophet that he awakens the morally living, not the dead-hearted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.anchor: what was discussed in the opening one is take up again in a different style

STUDYQURAN:36:77/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r1.claim: The drop from which the human is created means sperm, also described elsewhere as a draught of base fluid.
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r1.anchor: the creation of the human being from a drop (cf. 18:37; 22:5; 35:11; 40:67; 53:46; 75:37; 76:2; 80:19), meaning sperm

STUDYQURAN:36:77/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r2.claim: The creation of humans from a drop is cited as evidence of God's ability to resurrect them in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r2.anchor: is cited in several verses as testimony to God’s ability to resurrect human beings in the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:36:77/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r3.claim: For further discussion of human creation see 32:7–11, and for the stages of gestation see 22:5 and 23:14.
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r3.anchor: For the phases of gestation, see also 22:5; 23:14.

STUDYQURAN:36:77/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r4.claim: Failing to recognize one's own creation and what it testifies to makes one a manifest adversary to oneself.
STUDYQURAN:36:77/r4.anchor: in not recognizing the nature of one’s own creation and that to which it bears witness, one is a manifest adversary to oneself.

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r1.claim: This passage refutes denial of resurrection through the clearest evidence in human beings, just as the preceding passage refuted associating partners with God through evidence in what people possess.
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r1.anchor: كلام مستأنف مسوق لبيان بطلان إنكارهم البعث بعد ما شاهدوا في أنفسهم أوضح دلائله

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r2.claim: The hamza conveys denial and amazement; the wāw joins an omitted clause, and seeing here is inward or intellectual.
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r2.anchor: والهمزة للإنكار والتعجيب والواو للعطف على مقدر والرؤية قلبية

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r3.claim: Nutfa means clear water and is also used for a man's semen.
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r3.anchor: والنطفة الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r4.speaker: أبي بن خلف
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r4.claim: A group of Quraysh, including Ubayy ibn Khalaf, mocked resurrection; Ubayy crumbled a decayed bone before Muhammad, who answered that God would revive it, resurrect Ubayy, and put him in Hell.
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r4.anchor: روي أن جماعة من كفار قريش منهم أبي بن خلف ووهب بن حذافة بن جمع وأبو جهل والعاص بن وائل والوليد بن المغيرة اجتمعوا يوما

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r5.claim: The verse was revealed in reply to Ubayy's denial but applies to every human denier, since interpretation follows the general wording rather than the specific occasion.
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r5.anchor: فنزلت ردا عليه في إنكاره البعث لكنها عامة تصلح ردا لكل من ينكره من الإنسان لأن الاعتبار بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r6.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r6.claim: Al-Irshad explains that “the human” replaces a pronoun because the denial concerns human beings as such; the question calls any denier to certain knowledge of his creation from a lowly drop.
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r6.anchor: وإيراد الإنسان موضع المضمر لأن مدار الإنكار متعلق بأحواله من حيث هو إنسان

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r7.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r7.claim: A hadith says each person's creation is gathered in the womb for forty days as a drop, then for like periods as a clot and a morsel of flesh; an angel records four things including lifespan, provision, and whether the person is fortunate or wretched.
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r7.anchor: مصطفى عليه السلام كفت "إن خلق أحدكم يجمع في بطن أمه أربعين يوما نطفة ثم يكون علقة مثل ذلك

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r8.claim: God formed the person's shape, clothed him in human form, brought him from the womb to the world, nourished and endowed him with intellect, senses, heart, spirit, and powers of movement and speech.
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r8.anchor: آنكه تقطيع هيكل أو صورت شخص او در ظهور آورديم واورا كسوت بشريت وشانيديم وازان قرار مكين باين فضاى رحيب آورديم

BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p340#2/r9.claim: The human suddenly becomes a fierce disputant, either clear in his quarrel or making an argument apparent, despite his lowly origin.

BURSEVI:v7p341/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p341/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p341/r1.claim: The quoted poems compare the human to a pupil who turns against his teacher after learning archery or poetry, and to a raised puppy that bites its caretaker, illustrating the creature's ingratitude toward its maker.
BURSEVI:v7p341/r1.anchor: أعلمه الرماية كل يوم فلما اشتد ساعده رماني أعلمه القوافي كل حين فلما قال قافية هجاني

BURSEVI:v7p341/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p341/r2.speaker: السمرقندي
BURSEVI:v7p341/r2.claim: Al-Samarqandi says the operator of the surprise construction is the implicit sense of suddenness; it is followed by a nominal sentence, and can be construed as the sudden dispute itself or as encountering the dispute.
BURSEVI:v7p341/r2.anchor: قال السمرقندي : العامل في إذا المفاجأة معنى المفاجأة

TAB-FULL:v19p486/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r7.claim: The person who doubts resurrection forgets that God created him from a drop, then made him a fully formed disputant who argues against his Lord’s promise to revive the dead.
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r7.anchor: فتأويل الكلام إذن: أولم ير هذا الإنسان الذي يقول: {من يحيي العظام وهي رميم} [يس: 78] أنا خلقناه من نطفة فسويناه خلقا سويا {فإذا هو خصيم} [يس: 77] يقول: فإذا هو ذو خصومة لربه، يخاصمه فيما قال له ربه

TABATABAI:36:76-80/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r6.claim: The argument returns to resurrection, perhaps explaining the preceding reference to their speech. Seeing means certain knowledge; it is astonishing that a human made from a lowly drop becomes an explicit disputant.
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r6.anchor: والمراد بالرؤية العلم القطعي أي أولم يعلم الإنسان علما قاطعا أنا خلقناه من نطفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, Muqatil, and most commentators identify the disputing man as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬3): يريد أبي ابن خلف. وهو قول مقاتل (¬4)، والأكثرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r2.claim: Said ibn Jubayr identifies the man as al-As ibn Wa'il.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير (¬6): هو العاص بن وائل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan identifies him as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who disputed resurrection with the Prophet, crumbled a decayed bone, and asked whether God could revive it; the verse was revealed in response.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬7): هو أمية بن خلف، خاصم النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- في إنكار البعث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi rebukes the man's failure to reflect that he was made from a drop and then became an open disputant: he should consider his beginning and stop contesting resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p525#2/r4.anchor: يعني: ألا يرى أنه مخلوق من نطفة ثم هو يخاصم، وهذا تعجب من جهله وإنكار عليه خصومته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r4.claim: The human being in this verse is al-As ibn Wa'il.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r4.anchor: أنا خلقناه من نطفة } يعني: العاص بن وائل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r5.claim: An alternative identification of the human being is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r6.claim: He became an outspoken disputant arguing falsely with the Prophet against resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:74-78/r6.anchor: جدل بالباطل، خاصم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في إنكار البعث

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.claim: The passage exposes the contradiction of someone who neglects reflection on his own creation, then arrogantly judges the Creator's and Prophet's statements using reason alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.anchor: İnsanın kendi yaratılışı üzerinde düşünmeyi bir kenara bırakıp, küstahça bir tavırla yüce yaratıcının ve peygamberinin bildirdiklerini yalnızca aklıyla

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r2.claim: In Qur'anic usage, nutfa can mean male semen or a fertilized cell (zygote).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r2.anchor: Bunlardan nutfe, Kur’an’daki kullanımlarına göre erkeğin menisi veya döllenmiş hücre (zigot) mânasına gelmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r3.claim: If a person accepts the Creator's power to develop a seemingly insignificant drop into an adult, he should not doubt that the same power can revive a decayed bone; pagan Arabs also admitted God created the universe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r3.anchor: işte bu gücün çürümüş kemiğe de can verebileceğini yadırgamaması gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r4.claim: Makkan polytheists rejected Muhammad's prophethood and resurrection to preserve the established worship of other gods, and used mockery to influence people around them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r4.anchor: Resûlullah’ın peygamberliğini ve onun bildirdiklerini, dolayısıyla öldükten sonra dirilme gerçeğini kabul etmemek, sonuç olarak da Allah’ın yanı sıra başka mâbudlara tapma esasına dayalı kurulu düzenlerini sürdürmek için

QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r10.claim: God tightly joined, assembled, and proportioned human limbs and endowed people with reason and discrimination, yet the human becomes an explicit disputant who argues against divine rulings as if his own judgment were sound.
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r10.anchor: شدّدنا أسرهم ، وجمعنا نشرهم ، وسوينا أعضاءهم ، وركبنا أجزاءهم ، وأودعناهم العقل والتمييز

QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r11.claim: The human’s argumentative ingratitude is like the pupil who, after being taught archery until strong, turns his bow against his teacher.
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r11.anchor: أعلمه الرماية كل يوم . . . فلما اشتد ساعده رماني

QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r12.claim: Resurrection is no more difficult than initial creation; the One who produces fire in green branches can give life to rotten bones, and His ability to create a likeness is His ability to create the thing itself.
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r12.anchor: وقال إن الإعادة في معنى الإبداء ، فأي إشكال بقي في جواز الإعادة في الانتهاء

QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r13.claim: God revives souls after death as He creates humans from sperm and birds from eggs; He also gives believing hearts life through gnosis and kills unbelievers’ souls through desire and tyranny.
QUSHAYRI:v3p82/r13.anchor: وإنه يحيي النفوس بعد موتها في العرصة كما يحيي الإنسان من النطفة ، والطير من البيضة

ITQAN:v4p391/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r18.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p391/r18.claim: The human mentioned is identified as al-As ibn Wa'il.
ITQAN:v4p391/r18.anchor: هو العاص بن وائل وقيل أبي بن خلف وقيل أمية بن خلف

ITQAN:v4p391/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r19.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p391/r19.claim: An alternative identification is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
ITQAN:v4p391/r19.anchor: وقيل أبي بن خلف وقيل أمية بن خلف

ITQAN:v4p391/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r20.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p391/r20.claim: Another alternative identification is Umayya ibn Khalaf.
ITQAN:v4p391/r20.anchor: وقيل أبي بن خلف وقيل أمية بن خلف

DAMGHANI:v1p51/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r8.claim: Al-insān in the reminders about creation refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r8.anchor: التاسع عشر : الإنسان يعني أبي بن خلف الجمحي . قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n45/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n45/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n45/r1.claim: Razi, continuing his and Zamakhshari's reading at 16:4, takes khasim as the highest manifestation of the articulate, rational being.
ASAD-NOTES:36:77#n45/r1.anchor: Razi equates here the term khasim (lit., "contender in argument") with the highest manifestation of what is described as natiq

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r2.claim: The generic word “man” refers here to the Quraysh under discussion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r2.anchor: The word ُانَنسِإِ signify the Quraysh who are under discussion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r3.claim: Using the general term “man” expresses the author’s disgust with the Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r3.anchor: This general word is used to express disgust.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r5.claim: These verses continue the assurance in verse 76: arrogant Quraysh rival God, forget their creation and mock resurrection, just as they insult the Prophet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r5.anchor: These verses are connected to those before them through two aspects: It relates to the assurance sounded to the Prophet (sws) in the previous verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r6.claim: The earlier account of providence also leads to accountability: God’s favors entail gratitude and monotheism as well as a day of reward and punishment, which people evade.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p415/r6.anchor: providence entails gratitude and believing in one God, it also entails a day of reward and punishment.

NASHR:v1p484/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r3.claim: The written alif was deleted for abbreviation because of matching letters, not to avoid two sukūns; the proposed attribution of tarāy to Hishām is also unsound.
NASHR:v1p484/r3.anchor: كما زعم في (تراي) وليس في ذلك شيء يصح

NASHR:v2p77#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p77#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p77#2/r3.claim: Rāʾ takes imāla when an alif follows; after a connecting deletion the imāla remains, but not when jussive deletion removes the alif originally, as in awalam yara al-insān.
NASHR:v2p77#2/r3.anchor: أولم ير الإنسان لعدم وجود الألف بعد الراء

NASHR:v2p77#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p77#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p77#2/r4.claim: Rāʾ is singled out for imāla because its heaviness and strength from trilling distinguish it among letters that are inherently pronounced emphatically.
NASHR:v2p77#2/r4.anchor: من أجل ثقل الراء وقوتها بالتكرير تخصيصها من بين الحروف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r8.claim: The verse rebukes resurrection-deniers: a human made from a lowly drop, issued from an impure passage, disputes with God about reviving the dead despite having originated from lifeless matter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p83/r8.anchor: قبح تعالى إنكار الكفرة البعث، حيث قرر أن عنصره الذي خلق منه هو نطفة ماء مهين خارج من مخرج النجاسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the attribution to Ibn ʿAbbās that ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy b. Salūl brought the bone: the sūra and verse are unanimously Meccan, and Ibn Ubayy never made this migration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r1.anchor: ووهم من نسب إلى ابن عباس أن الجائي بالعظم هو عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r2.claim: Stages between creation from a drop and becoming a clear disputant are elided; much is supplied by 23:13, and the later phrase describes the discrimination and speech that make disputation possible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r2.anchor: بين قوله: فإذا هو خصيم مبين وبين: خلقناه من نطفة، جمل محذوفة تبين أكثرها في قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r3.claim: After beginning as a drop, the human becomes discerning, articulate, capable of disputation, and able to express what is within.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r3.anchor: أي فإذا هو بعد ما كان نطفة، رجل مميز منطيق قادر على الخصام، مبين معرب عما في نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r1.claim: This passage disproves resurrection denial from what people observe in themselves, just as the preceding argument disproved associating partners from signs in their possessions.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r1.anchor: مسوق لبيان بطلان إنكارهم البعث بعد ما شاهدوا في أنفسهم ما يوجب التصديق به

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r2.claim: A proposed reading treats the verse as consolation to the Prophet about their words, like 36:76; al-Alusi says that does not fit.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنه تسلية له عليه الصلاة والسلام كقوله تعالى ( فلا يحزنك قولهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r3.claim: The hamza conveys denial and wonder; the waw coordinates with an implied sentence that entails the question, as in the earlier question at 36:71.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r3.anchor: والهمزة للإنكار والتعجب والواو للعطف على جملة مقدرة هي مستتبعة للمعطوف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r4.claim: The question may repeat the previous denial rhetorically and prepare a stronger one: people should know their own creation, the clearest and most important fact about themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r4.anchor: أو هي عين تلك الجملة أعيدت تأكيدا للنكير السابق وتمهيدا لإنكار ما هو أحق منه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r5.claim: The scholars link both questions through inversion: God made provision for people to be thanked but they disbelieved, and made them from lowly fluid for humility but they became arrogant and disputatious.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r5.anchor: فإنه تعالى خلق للإنسان ما خلق ليشكر فكفر وجحد المنعم والنعم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r6.claim: The generic word human is used rather than a pronoun because the question concerns human nature and behavior.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r6.anchor: وإيراد الإنسان مورد الضمير لأن مدار الإنكار متعلق بأحواله من حيث هو إنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r7.claim: The phrase presents the human as suddenly becoming an emphatic, open disputant in false argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53/r7.anchor: أي مبالغ في الخصومة والجدال الباطل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r1.claim: God created humans from something low and vile, yet they suddenly dispute a matter whose truth their own origin plainly witnesses.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r1.anchor: ظاهر متجاهر في ذلك عطف على الجملة المنفية داخل في حيز الإنكار والتعجب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r2.claim: Mubin is transitive, describing a disputant who makes his inner thoughts clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r2.anchor: مبين ) متعد والكلام من متممات شواهد صحة البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r3.speaker: ابن مردويه
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r3.claim: A narration attributed to Ibn Abbas through Ibn Mardawayh identifies the challenger as Ubayy ibn Khalaf, whom the Prophet killed at Uhud with a spear; Abu Malik, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Suddi, Ikrima, and others report that identification.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r3.anchor: وفي رواية ابن مردوية عنه أن الجاني القائل ذلك أبي بن خلف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r4.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r4.claim: Other reports from Ibn Abbas name Abu Jahl or Abd Allah ibn Ubay; Abu Hayyan rejects the latter attribution because the sura is Meccan and Abd Allah ibn Ubay never made such an open challenge.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r4.anchor: وفي رواية أخرة عن الحبر أنه أبو جهل بن هشام وفي أخرى عنه أيضا أنه عبد الله بن أبي

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan chooses Ubayy ibn Khalaf as the soundest identification, while allowing each named unbeliever may have made the challenge.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r5.anchor: والذي اختاره وادعى أنه أصح الأقوال أنه أبي بن خلف ثم قال : ويحتمل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r6.claim: Mujahid and Qatada are also reported to identify Umayya ibn Khalaf as the challenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r6.anchor: وحكى عن مجاهد وقتادة أنه أمية بن خلف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r7.claim: An alternative reads this as the sudden result of creation: after insignificant fluid, the human becomes discerning and eloquent, able to argue.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r7.anchor: فإذا هو بعدما كان ماء مهينا رجل مميز منطيق قادر على الخصام

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r8.claim: On that reading, the clause coordinates with created him, the sudden transition refers to creation, and mubin is transitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r8.anchor: فهو حينئذ معطوف على خلقناه والتعقيب والمفاجأة ناظران إلى خلقه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r9.claim: The nominal sentence marks persistent disputation; the suddenness intensifies astonishment at that transformation.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r9.anchor: إسمية للدلالة على استقراره في الخصومة واستمراره عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r10.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r10.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says al-As ibn Wa'il brought the Prophet a decayed bone, crumbled it, and asked whether God could revive it; the Prophet said God would raise it, then cause him to die, revive him, and enter him into Hell, whereupon these verses to the sura's end were revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p53#2/r10.anchor: أخرج جماعة منهم الضياء في المختارة عن ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p28#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p28#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p28#2/r3.claim: The human is made from a drop, yet becomes an obvious contentious disputant; he should reflect on his beginning and stop arguing against resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p28#2/r3.anchor: أنه مخلوق من نطفة ثم يخاصم فكيف لا يتفكر في بدء خلقه حتى يدع الخصومة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p28#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p28#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p28#2/r4.claim: The verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who challenged the Prophet with a decayed bone and asked whether God would revive it; the Prophet answered yes, saying Ubayy would also be raised and enter Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p28#2/r4.anchor: نزلت في أبي بن خلف الجمحي خاصم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في إنكار البعث، وأتاه بعظم قد بلي ففتته بيده،

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r6.claim: The reminder of humanity's creation from a drop is a second consolation; denial of resurrection is especially ugly since it denies God's power over what is easier than the first creation and repays an immense gift with disobedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r6.anchor: تسلية ثانية بتهوين ما يقولونه بالنسبة إلى إنكارهم الحشر

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r7.claim: In the reported encounter, Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet a decayed bone and crumbled it, asking whether God could revive it; the Prophet answered yes, saying He would raise Ubayy and cast him into Hell, and the verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r7.anchor:
فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام:
" نعم ويبعثك ويدخلك النار فنزلت "

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r8.claim: Another explanation is that, after being contemptible fluid, a person becomes distinct, articulate, and capable of arguing about what is within him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:76-77/r8.anchor: فإذا هو بعد ما كان ماء مهينا مميز منطيق قادر على الخصام

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r1.claim: After the earlier proof that God changes a person from one condition to another, and the affirmation of His encompassing knowledge, the text gives a clearer argument for resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r1.anchor: ولما أثبت سبحانه بهذا الدليل قدرته على ما هدد به أولا من التحويل من حال إلى أخرى , فثبتت بذلك قدرته على البعث

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r2.claim: Here seeing means knowing with a certainty and obviousness comparable to seeing with one's eyes.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r2.anchor: أي يعلم علما هو في ظهوره كالمحسوس بالبصر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r3.claim: Al-insān denotes the human species, including this particular opponent and others, although one individual was the occasion for the verse.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r3.anchor: أي جنسه منهم ومن غيرهم وإن كان الذي نزلت فيه واحدا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r4.claim: Humanity began as a tiny, contemptible drop of water with no use, while God had created the human's father from soil and mother from flesh and bones.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r4.anchor: شيء يسير حقير من ماء لا انتفاع به بعد إبداعنا أباه من تراب وأمه من لحم وعظام

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r5.claim: The sudden turn from a lowly origin to an articulate adversary is astonishing: the human uses God-given reason, power, and speech to dispute God's messengers and people dear to Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r5.anchor: من أعطاء العقل والقدرة في قدرته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r6.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r6.claim: Al-Qushayri quotes a poem illustrating how a pupil trained in archery turns his skill against his teacher once strong.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p284/r6.anchor: أنشد الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري في ذلك : أعلمه الرماية كل يوم فلما اشتد ساعدوه رماني

DURR-FULL:v7p73/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p73/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p73/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-As ibn Waʾil brought a weathered bone, crushed it, and challenged the Prophet about its resurrection; the Prophet answered that God would resurrect it, then cause al-As to die and enter Hell, and the closing verses of Ya-Sin were revealed.
DURR-FULL:v7p73/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: جاء العاص بن وائل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم حائل ففته بيده فقال يا محمد

DURR-FULL:v7p73/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p73/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p73/r10.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas says Abdullah ibn Abi broke a weathered bone before the Prophet and asked how God could raise it after decay; the Prophet answered that God would resurrect it and send him to Hell.
DURR-FULL:v7p73/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال جاء عبد الله بن أبي وفي يده عظم حائل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فكسره بيده ثم قال: يا محمد كيف يبعثه الله وهو رميم

DURR-FULL:v7p75/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the passage about man's creation from a drop was revealed about Ubayy, who crumbled a weathered bone and was told God would kill and resurrect him before casting him into the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r1.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {أو لم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة} قال: نزلت في أبي بن خلف

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil brought the Prophet a dried bone, crumbled it, and asked whether God could revive it; the Prophet said God would resurrect him, then punish him, and the verses through the end of Yā Sīn were revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله ، عنهما قال : جاء العاصي بن وائل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم حائل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who crumbled a decayed bone before the Prophet and challenged his account of its future resurrection; the Prophet affirmed it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3202/r3.anchor: عن السدى رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : أو لم ير الانسان انا خلقناه من نطفة قال : نزلت في أبي بن خلف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r1.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the verse was revealed when al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi brought a decayed bone to the Prophet, crumbled it, and asked who could revive it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r1.anchor: قال فيها ابن جبير: إنها نزلت بسبب أن المعاصي بن وائل السهمي جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم رميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r7.claim: The reply establishes the proof that a person who began as a sperm can become an articulate disputant; this first creation is itself a revival after nonexistence and lack of life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r7.anchor: ثم نزلت الآية مبينة ومقيمة للحجة في أن الإنسان نطفة ثم يكون بعد ذلك خصيما مبينا هل هذا إلا إحياء بعد موت وعدم حياة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, says the verse concerns al-As ibn Wa'il, who crushed a bone and asked whether God could revive it; the Prophet said God would revive him after death and place him in Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه العاص بن وائل السهمي أخذ عظما من البطحاء ففته بيده ثم قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r2.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r2.claim: Al-Awfi transmits from Ibn Abbas that the disputant was Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and a similar incident occurred with him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول جرى له نحو هذه القصة رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r3.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that the disputant was Abu Jahl and that the incident happened to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r3.anchor: والثالث أنه أبو جهل ابن هشام وأن هذه القصة جرت له رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r4.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the disputant as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r4.anchor: والرابع أنه أمية بن خلف قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r5.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r5.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and most exegetes identify the disputant as Ubayy ibn Khalaf, whose bone-crushing challenge is the reported occasion; Ibn al-Jawzi notes that commentators follow this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r5.anchor: والخامس أنه أبي بن خلف الجمحي وهذه القصة جرت له قاله مجاهد وقتادة والجمهور وعليه المفسرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r6.claim: The verse marvels at the disputant's ignorance in denying resurrection: he should reflect on his own origin and stop arguing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r6.anchor: ومعنى الكلام التعجب من جهل هذا المخاصم في إنكاره البعث والمعنى ألا يعلم أنه مخلوق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r7.claim: An alternative says the verse reminds him of God's favor in creating him from a drop and making him a disputant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p40/r7.anchor: وقيل هذا تنبيه له على نعمة الله عليه حيث أنشأه من نطفة فصار مجادلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد، وعكرمة، وعروة بن الزبير، والسدي، وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.claim: These authorities report that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to Muhammad with a decayed bone, crumbled and scattered it, and challenged whether God would resurrect it; the final verses of Yasin were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد، وعكرمة، وعروة بن الزبير، والسدي. وقتادة: جاء أبي بن خلف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says al-Asi ibn Waʾil took a bone from al-Batha, crushed it, and asked Muhammad whether God could revive it; Muhammad said God would resurrect and send him to Hell, and Yasin's closing verses were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير (6) ، عن ابن عباس، أن العاصي (7) بن وائل أخذ عظما من البطحاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits the al-Asi ibn Waʾil report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr but does not name Ibn Abbas in its chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.anchor: ورواه ابن جرير عن يعقوب بن إبراهيم، عن هشيم، عن أبي بشر، عن سعيد بن جبير، فذكره ولم يذكر "ابن عباس"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.claim: Al-Awfi's report names Abdullah ibn Ubayy as the visitor, but Ibn Kathir rejects it as munkar because Yasin is Meccan and Ibn Ubayy was in Medina.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.anchor: وروي من طريق العوفي، عن ابن عباس قال: جاء عبد الله بن أبي بعظم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r5.claim: Whether the occasion involved Ubayy ibn Khalaf, al-Asi ibn Waʾil, or both, the passage applies generally to everyone who denies resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r5.anchor: وعلى كل تقدير سواء كانت هذه الآيات قد نزلت في أبي بن خلف، أو [في] (2) العاص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r6.claim: The definite article in 'the human' is generic and encompasses every denier of resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r6.anchor: والألف واللام في قوله: {أولم ير الإنسان} للجنس، يعم كل (4) منكر للبعث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r1.claim: Humanity's beginning from a lowly, weak drop proves that the One who created it can restore it after death; the text links this argument to other descriptions of human creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r1.anchor: فإن الله ابتدأ خلق الإنسان من سلالة من ماء مهين، فخلقه من شيء حقير ضعيف مهين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r2.speaker: بسر بن جحاش
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r2.claim: Ahmad reports the Prophet's divine saying to Adam's child: God created, proportioned, and clothed him from a tiny origin; when death reaches the throat he asks to give charity too late. Ibn Majah also transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r2.anchor: عن بسر ابن جحاش؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بصق يوما في كفه

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.claim: A polytheist brought a crumbled old bone and challenged Muhammad about God reviving it; the passage from this verse to the sūra’s end was revealed.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.anchor: قيل: جاء مشرك بعظم بال متفتت، وقال: يا محمد، أتزعم أن الله يبعث هذا بعدما بلي؟ فقال: نعم، فنزلت الآية

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r12.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies the human disputant as al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil al-Sahmi.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r12.anchor: فقيل: العاص بن وائل السهمي، عن سعيد بن جبير

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r13.speaker: قتادة، ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r13.claim: Qatada and Mujahid identify the disputant as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r13.anchor: وقيل: أبي بن خلف، عن قتادة، ومجاهد

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r14.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r14.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the disputant as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r14.anchor: وقيل: أمية بن خلف، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the disputant as ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r15.anchor: وقيل: عبد الله بن أبي، عن ابن عباس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r1.claim: The passage rebukes denial of resurrection with extraordinary force, exposing persistent unbelief, ingratitude, baseness, and insolence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r1.anchor: قبح الله عز وجل إنكارهم البعث تقبيحا لا ترى أعجب منه وأبلغ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r2.claim: It recalls that the disputant came from semen, the lowliest and filthiest origin, then marvels that he arrogantly disputes with the Almighty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r2.anchor: عنصره الذي خلقه منه هو أخس شيء وأمهنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r3.claim: The man rides falsehood and persists in arguing that no one can revive decayed bones, although he himself arose from lifeless matter; this is brazen contradiction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#2/r3.anchor: ثم يكون خصامه في ألزم وصف له وألصقه به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r1.speaker: أبي بن خلف
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r1.claim: A report says Ubayy ibn Khalaf, with Abu Jahl, al-Asi ibn Wa'il, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, challenged Muhammad by crushing a decayed bone; the Prophet answered that God would revive him and cast him into Hell.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r1.anchor: فقال لهم أبي : ألا ترون إلى ما يقول محمد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r2.claim: After being insignificant fluid, a person becomes distinct, articulate, and capable of argument; مبين means able to express what is within.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r2.anchor: فإذا هو بعد ما كان ماء مهينا رجل مميز منطبق قادر على الخصام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p34/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p34/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p34/r1.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet calls Yā Sīn the Qurʾān’s heart and promises forgiveness and reward like reciting the Qurʾān twenty-two times for reciting it sincerely.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p34/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 943 ) ( إن لكل شيء قلبا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p34/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p34/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p34/r2.claim: A second report attributed to the Prophet says Yā Sīn intercedes for its reciter and brings forgiveness to its listener; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p34/r2.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( 944 ) ( إن في القرآن سورة يشفع قارئها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r1.claim: Ikrima, Mujahid, and al-Suddi say it concerns Ubayy ibn Khalaf disputing resurrection with the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r1.anchor: في بعث الموتى ، قاله عكرمة ومجاهد والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports al-As ibn Wa'il crumbling a bone and questioning resurrection; the Prophet said God would revive him, then kill and resurrect him and put him in Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.anchor: فنزلت هذه الآيات فيه ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r3.claim: Khaseem mubin means an open disputant who presents his argument clearly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r3.anchor: أي مجادل في الخصومة مبين للحجة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r4.claim: His transformation from nonexistence into a disputant reminds him of God's favor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r4.anchor: أن ينبهه بذلك على نعمه عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r5.claim: It points to resurrection, since God first created him from nothing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r5.anchor: أن يدله بذلك على إحياء الموتى كما ابتدأه بعد أن لم يكن شيئا

MUQATIL:36:76-78/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r2.claim: The passage arose over Ubayy ibn Khalaf's challenge: Meccan leaders heard Muhammad's resurrection claim, and Ubayy brought him a rotten bone, crumbled and scattered it, and asked who could revive it. Muhammad answered that God would revive it, then kill and resurrect Ubayy and admit him to Hell.
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r2.anchor: أن أبا جهل، والوليد بن المغيرة، وعتبة وشيبة ابنى ربيعة، وعقبة، والعاص بن وائل، كانوا جلوسا، فقال لهم أبى بن خلف

MUQATIL:36:76-78/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r3.claim: Did the human not know God created him from a drop, yet he became an openly disputatious opponent over resurrection?
MUQATIL:36:76-78/r3.anchor: { أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين } [آية: 77] بين الخصومة فيما يخاصم النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم عن البعث

NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r1.claim: The drop is filthy fluid emitted from the urethra, the channel of impurity.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r1.anchor: مذرة خارجة من الاحليل الذى هو قناه النجاسة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r2.claim: Though from a lowly origin, a person openly disputes with his Lord and denies the power to revive decayed bones, the sort of lifeless matter from which he came.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r2.anchor: فهو على مهانة أصله ودناءة أوله يتصدى لمخاصمة ربه وينكر قدرته على إحياء الميت بعد مارمت عظامه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r3.claim: His denial is extreme stubbornness: he disputes resurrection from dead matter despite himself originating from lifeless matter.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p14#6/r3.anchor: ثم يكون خصامه فى ألزم وصف له وألصقه به وهو كونه منشأ من موات وهو ينكر انشاءه من موات

QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the disputatious man as Abdullah ibn Ubayy.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الإنسان هو عبد الله بن أبي. وقال سعيد بن جبير

QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies him as al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو العاص بن وائل السهمي. وقال الحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r3.speaker: الحسن وابن إسحاق ومالك
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Ishaq, and Malik identify him as Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi; Ibn Wahb transmits the report from Malik.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو أبي بن خلف الجمحي. وقاله ابن إسحاق، ورواه ابن وهب عن مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r4.claim: A nutfa is a small amount of water; the verb natafa means to drip.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r4.anchor: وهو اليسير من الماء نطف إذا قطر. { فإذا هو خصيم مبين }

QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r5.claim: He becomes a clear, articulate disputant who presents an argument in controversy, though he had previously been nothing mentioned.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r5.anchor: أي مجادل في الخصومة مبين للحجة. يريد بذلك أنه صار بعد أن لم يكن شيئا مذكورا

QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r6.claim: A report says the man brought Muhammad a decayed bone and asked whether God could revive it. Muhammad answered yes, saying God would resurrect the questioner and admit him to Hell; the verse was then revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:77/r6.anchor: وذلك أنه أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم حائل فقال: يا محمد أترى أن الله يحيي هذا بعد ما رم
